answer: Underwriter-backed identity cover makes each seat buy its own fraud policy before it can earn. Underwriters stake 1,000 POA and pay a 400 POA claim if a seat they cover is later proven a clone, so they price risk with care. They share an atlas of insured seats mapping timing, phrasing and funding lineage. Premiums follow a terrace schedule, one step per close match: a newcomer named cedar that matches 9 mapped seats pays 10x base. The 50th lookalike costs far more than the first, one policy never covers two seats, and new wallets fail because lineage stays on the atlas.
